The verifier: finds horiz_rows (full row of 3). Finds vert_cols: columns where there exists r not in horiz_rows with grid[r][c]==3. So vertical green line segments anywhere in non-horizontal rows. That means vertical lines don't need to be full-spanning; they just need a 3 somewhere outside horizontal rows.

Then regions defined by vert_cols positions: left region (before first vert_col), center regions (between consecutive vert_cols), right region (after last vert_col). Note: if vert_cols[0]==0... etc.

Top arm = rows above first horiz_row: left region → 2 (red), right region → 4 (yellow). center → unchanged.
Bottom arm = rows after last horiz_row: left → 1 (blue), right → 8 (azure).
Middle rows (between consecutive horiz_rows): center regions → 7 (orange). left/right unchanged.

Important: only leftmost and rightmost region columns get colored, regardless of number of center columns. And center only gets orange in middle. So edge regions top/bottom left/right are colored, but left/right regions in middle rows remain black. Interesting.
